title: Saying who you are and where you're from
es: Soy Tomás. Soy de Toronto. ¿Y tú, de dónde eres?
en: I'm Tomás. I'm from Toronto. And you, where are you from?

title: Reading Spanish aloud: five vowels, the letters that surprise you, and the stress mark
es: Mi mamá toma café.
note: Text-only: describe sounds against English; teach the written accent as a typing skill the checker will hold them to. Frame: café, mamá, teléfono, perro / pero, jugo, calle
en: My mum drinks coffee.

forms.en: My mum drinks coffee.

forms.es: Tengo un perro, pero no tengo gato.
forms.en: I've got a dog, but I haven't got a cat.
Do you want a juice?

forms.es: Mi teléfono está en la mesa.
forms.en: My phone is on the table.
I live on this street.

title: Every noun is "el" or "la": the, a, and how to guess which
es: el café, la mesa, un carro, una ciudad, el día, la mano
en: the coffee, the table, a car, a city, the day, the hand
note: Flag el día, la mano, el problema, la foto. Always teach nouns with their article from here on.

title: Talking about what you do: -ar verbs (hablo, hablas, habla)
es: Trabajo en un café. ¿Hablas inglés? Vale cocina muy bien.
en: I work in a café. Do you speak English? Vale cooks very well.
note: Ustedes forms only; vosotros never produced.

title: The other regular verbs: -er and -ir (como, vivo)
es: Vivo en Bogotá. Comemos a la una. ¿Lees en español?
en: I live in Bogotá. We eat at one. Do you read in Spanish?

title: Where something is and how someone is: estar
es: El café está en La Candelaria. ¿Cómo estás? Estoy cansado.
en: The café is in La Candelaria. How are you? I'm tired.
note: Only location and a small set of states (bien, mal, cansado, enfermo, feliz). ser vs estar with adjectives comes at A2 (g:ser-estar-adjectives).

title: Describing people and things: alto, alta, simpáticos, inteligente
es: Mi hermana es alta y muy simpática.
en: My sister is tall and very nice.

forms.es: Mi hermana es alta y muy simpática.
forms.en: My sister is tall and very nice.
The buñuelos are delicious.
Mariana is Colombian.
The arepas are good.

note: Plurals of nouns and adjectives together; adjective after the noun by default. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 40 to 15 (u02). Agreement is A1 core and gender is session 6: Vale está cansada, Mariana es colombiana, las arepas son buenas.

title: Asking questions: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto, por qué
es: ¿Dónde vives? ¿Cuántos años tienes? ¿Por qué estás aquí?
en: Where do you live? How old are you? Why are you here?
note: ¿ ? marks, accents on question words, intonation questions (¿Tienes hambre?).

title: Saying what you like: me gusta, me gustan, ¿te gusta?
es: Me gusta el café. No me gustan los lunes. ¿Te gusta bailar?
en: I like coffee. I don't like Mondays. Do you like dancing?
note: Unpacks c:me-gusta. Only me/te here; le/les/nos and encantar/doler in g:gustar-full.

title: Verbs that change inside: quiero, puedo, prefiero, duermo (the "boot" verbs)
es: ¿Quieres un tinto? No puedo hoy. Prefiero el té. Duermo poco.
en: Do you want a coffee? I can't today. I prefer tea. I sleep little.
note: e→ie and o→ue (and jugar u→ue). Unpacks c:quiero and c:puedo. e→i comes later (g:stem-e-i). Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): tener's forms are a chunk from session 14 (c:tienes).

title: Verb + verb: quiero ir, puedo pagar, necesito dormir, tengo que trabajar
es: ¿Quieres tomar algo?
en: Do you want something to drink?

forms.en: Do you want something to drink?

forms.es: Hoy no puedo salir: tengo que trabajar.
forms.en: I can't go out today: I have to work.
Dancing is really great.
I need to sleep.

note: saber + inf = know how to; poder = be able / be allowed. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 72 to 24 (u03), straight after the boot verbs whose forms it uses (SEQ day 28; the c:quiero / c:puedo / c:tengo-que chunks start it in week 1). Covers querer, poder, preferir, necesitar, tener que and hay que + infinitive, and a plain infinitive as subject (Bailar es divertido) and empezar a / terminar de. saber + infinitive waits for g:yo-irregular (p:saber-conocer); volver a, dejar de, soler and ponerse a are tagged to their own patterns.

title: Talking about plans: voy a + verb
es: Voy a abrir el café el lunes. ¿Qué vas a hacer mañana?
en: I'm going to open the café on Monday. What are you going to do tomorrow?
note: Unpacks c:voy-a. Ir a is THE future of everyday Latin American Spanish; the -ré future is taught later for guesses and promises. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-ir-a-infinitivo-a1.

title: Saying what you did: -ar verbs in the past (hablé, hablaste, habló)
es: Ayer trabajé hasta las nueve. ¿Compraste el pan? Vale cerró temprano.
en: Yesterday I worked until nine. Did you buy the bread? Vale closed early.
note: LatAm: the preterite is THE past, including for today (Hoy trabajé mucho). Unpacks c:compre-trabaje. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: The past of -er and -ir verbs (comí, viviste, salió)
es: Comí arepas. ¿Saliste anoche? Simón aprendió una palabra nueva.
en: I ate arepas. Did you go out last night? Simón learned a new word.
note: Unpacks c:comi. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: The three past forms you'll use most: fui, fue, hice
es: Fui al mercado. Fue un desastre. ¿Qué hiciste el sábado?
en: I went to the market. It was a disaster. What did you do on Saturday?
note: fui = I went AND I was; context decides. Unpacks c:fui and c:que-hiciste. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-indefinido-irregular-a2. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Verbs with an odd "I" form: tengo, hago, salgo, conozco, sé
es: Tengo dos hermanos. Salgo a las seis. No conozco a nadie aquí. No sé.
en: I have two brothers. I leave at six. I don't know anyone here. I don't know.
note: Unpacks c:tengo and c:no-se. tener also e→ie (tienes, tiene). SEQ new lesson(s): gr-presente-yo-irregular-a1. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): hago / salgo / vengo / pongo / traigo ride as a chunk family from session 22 (c:hago-salgo-vengo), when u03 teaches salir and venir; tengo from session 3 (c:tengo); sé from 11 (c:no-se).

title: Whose is it, the whole set: mi, mis, tu, tus, su, sus, nuestro, nuestra
es: Mi abuela tenía un café.
en: My grandmother had a café.

forms.en: My grandmother had a café.
Does your sister live in Medellín?
His dog is huge.
Our house is small.

note: su = his/her/their/your (usted); disambiguate with de él / de ella. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): mi / tu / su + noun are licensed from session 12 by p:possessives-basic; this lesson (40, was 44) systematises nuestro/a/os/as agreement and the four meanings of su (de él, de ella, de usted, de ellos).

title: Saying no to everything: nada, nadie, nunca, tampoco, ningún
es: No hay nadie.
en: There's nobody here.

forms.en: There's nobody here.
I never eat meat.

I'm not hungry.
Me neither.
I don't know anything.

note: Double negative is required (no… nada). también/tampoco. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 69 to 44 (u05). no hay nada / no hay nadie / no sé nada ride as a chunk from session 23 (c:no-hay-nada), algo / alguien as p:indefinites-basic (23).

title: Setting the scene in the past: era, estaba, tenía, había
es: El café era pequeño. Había una mesa al lado de la ventana. Mi abuela tenía sesenta años.
en: The café was small. There was a table by the window. My grandmother was sixty.
note: Only state verbs (ser, estar, tener, haber, querer, saber, poder). Full imperfect at g:imperfect-habitual. Unpacks c:era. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-imperfecto-estados-a1. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Irregular pasts: tuve, estuve, pude, puse, vine, quise, dije, traje
es: Tuve que salir. Estuvimos dos horas en el trancón. No pude dormir. ¿Qué te dijo?
en: I had to leave. We were in the traffic jam for two hours. I couldn't sleep. What did he tell you?
note: Teach the shared endings (-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron; dijeron/trajeron). Includes dar/ver. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-indefinido-irregular-a2. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: How long ago: hace + time
es: Llegué hace dos semanas. Mi abuela abrió el café hace cuarenta años.
en: I arrived two weeks ago. My grandmother opened the café forty years ago.
note: Also hace + time + que + present (Hace un mes que vivo aquí) as a frame. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: "There is" vs "it's there": hay un banco, el banco está
es: Hay una panadería en la esquina.
en: There's a bakery on the corner.

forms.es: Hay una panadería en la esquina.
forms.en: There's a bakery on the corner.

forms.es: La panadería está al lado del café.
forms.en: The bakery is next to the café.

forms.es: Hay dos bancos en esta calle.
forms.en: There are two banks on this street.
The bank is nearby.

note: hay + un/una/numbers/nothing; está/están + el/la/names. hay is never plural (hay dos).

title: This, that, that one over there: este, ese, aquel (and esto, eso)
es: Este apartamento es caro. ¿Y ese? ¿Qué es eso?
en: This apartment is expensive. And that one? What is that?
note: ese covers most "that" in speech; aquel for far away and far back in time. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): este / esta / esto / eso are licensed from session 14 by p:demonstratives-basic; this lesson is the three distances (este, ese, aquel) with aquí / ahí / allá.

title: How much and how many: mucho, poco, bastante, demasiado, and muy vs mucho
es: Hay mucha gente.
en: There are a lot of people.

forms.en: There are a lot of people.
The rent is very expensive.
I have too many things.
I work quite a lot.

note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): muy / mucho / poco are licensed from session 12 by p:quantifiers-basic; this lesson is bastante, demasiado, and muy vs mucho as a system.

title: Have you ever…? Experience and "not yet": he estado, todavía no he…
es: ¿Has estado en Cartagena?
en: Have you been to Cartagena?

forms.en: Have you been to Cartagena?
I've never tried ajiaco.

forms.es: Todavía no he visto el contrato.
forms.en: I haven't seen the contract yet.

note: LatAm scope ONLY: life experience (alguna vez, nunca), ya / todavía no, and situations still open. Never for finished events today: Hoy fui al banco, not Hoy he ido. Unpacks c:has-estado. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: What's happening right now: estoy trabajando
es: Estoy trabajando, te llamo luego. ¿Qué estás haciendo?
en: I'm working, I'll call you later. What are you doing?
note: Use only for right-now/temporary; plain present for habits and many "now" uses. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 78 to 69 (u08; SEQ day 54): ¿Qué estás haciendo? is everyday A1.

title: Not repeating the noun: lo, la, los, las (and the personal a)
es:
¿El jugo?
Lo quiero sin azúcar.
en:
The juice?
I want it without sugar.

forms.en:
The juice?
I want it without sugar.
Do you know Vale? I met her yesterday.
The keys, where did you leave them?

note: lo/la standard (no leísmo). Comprehension first: "who did what to whom?" (Lo ve María). PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 92 to 72 (u08; SEQ day 75): ¿Lo has probado? — No, nunca lo he probado. me / te / nos as objects are licensed from session 30 by p:me-te-nos-objects; this lesson is lo / la / los / las and the personal a.

title: Your daily routine: me levanto, te duchas, se acuesta
es: Me levanto a las cinco. Vale se acuesta tarde. ¿A qué hora te despiertas?
en: I get up at five. Vale goes to bed late. What time do you wake up?
note: Unpacks c:me-llamo. Pronoun before the conjugated verb; attached to the infinitive (voy a levantarme).

title: Before leaving, after eating, on arriving: antes de, después de, al + verb
es: Antes de salir, cierra la puerta. Después de comer, tomamos tinto. Al llegar, me llamas.
en: Before leaving, close the door. After eating, we have coffee. When you arrive, call me.
note: Spanish uses the infinitive where English uses -ing. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 156 (A2) to 78 (u09): antes de / después de + infinitive is how a routine is told (Antes de dormir, leo).

title: Have to, must, no need: tener que vs hay que vs deber, and no tienes que
es: Tienes que descansar.
en: You have to rest.

forms.en: You have to rest.
You have to pay first. (in general)
You should go to the doctor.
You don't have to come tomorrow.

note: Unpacks c:tengo-que and c:hay-que. no tener que = don't have to (not "must not"). SEQ new lesson(s): gr-tener-que-hay-que-a1. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): tener que / hay que + infinitive are licensed from session 24 by g:verb-infinitive (chunks from session 6). This lesson (still 82) contrasts personal and general obligation with deber (present), and no tener que (no need) vs no deber (mustn't). The tagger now maps deber + infinitive here (it was B1 g:deber-modal).

title: Likes for everyone: le gusta, nos encanta, les interesa, and a mí también
es: A Vale le encantan los buñuelos.
en: Vale loves buñuelos.

forms.es: A Vale le encantan los buñuelos.
forms.en: Vale loves buñuelos.

forms.es:
A mí no me gusta el picante.
A mí tampoco.
forms.en:
I don't like spicy food.
Me neither.
We're very interested in history.
My head hurts.

note: encantar, interesar, importar, doler (me duele la cabeza). Reading practice so learners don't read le as the subject. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-pronombres-me-te-nos-a1.

title: More inside-changers: pido, sirvo, sigo, repito
es: Siempre pido lo mismo. ¿Me repites? Aquí sirven el mejor ajiaco.
en: I always order the same thing. Can you repeat that? They serve the best ajiaco here.

title: After for, with, to: para mí, contigo, sin ti
es: ¿Esto es para mí? ¿Vienes conmigo? Sin ti no puedo.
en: Is this for me? Are you coming with me? I can't without you.
note: PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 130 to 92 (u10: Para mí, un tinto. ¿Y para ti?). a mí también / ¿y a ti? are a chunk from session 21 (c:a-mi-tambien), with gustar.

title: What used to happen: the full "used to" past (trabajaba, comía, vivía)
es: De niño iba al café todos los domingos. Mi abuela cocinaba y yo comía.
en: As a kid I used to go to the café every Sunday. My grandmother cooked and I ate.
note: Only three irregulars: ser, ir, ver. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Past-tense surprises: busqué, llegué, empecé, leyó, pidió, durmió
es: Llegué tarde. Busqué las llaves. Vale pidió un aumento. Don Hernando se durmió.
en: I arrived late. I looked for the keys. Vale asked for a raise. Don Hernando fell asleep.
note: SEQ new lesson(s): gr-indefinido-irregular-a2. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Comparing: más… que, menos… que, tan… como, mejor, peor
es: Bogotá es más fría que Medellín.
en: Bogotá is colder than Medellín.

forms.es: Bogotá es más fría que Medellín.
forms.en: Bogotá is colder than Medellín.

forms.es: Este café es mejor que el otro.
forms.en: This coffee is better than the other one.

forms.es: No es tan caro como dicen.
forms.en: It's not as expensive as they say.

note: mayor/menor for age. más de + number. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Two pasts in one story: what happened vs what things were like
es: Era tarde y llovía. De repente alguien tocó la puerta.
en: It was late and it was raining. Suddenly someone knocked on the door.
note: Blocked here, then interleaved across sessions; one of the big five, recycled to C1. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Was doing it when…: estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono
es: Estaba cerrando el café cuando llegó el señor Altamira.
en: I was closing the café when Mr Altamira arrived.

forms.es: Estaba cerrando el café cuando llegó el señor Altamira.
forms.en: I was closing the café when Mr Altamira arrived.

forms.es: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
forms.en: I was cooking when the phone rang.
What were you doing when I called you?

note: PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Saying what you think, know and heard: creo que, sé que, dice que
es: Creo que tienes razón. Dice que viene mañana. Sabía que ibas a decir eso.
en: I think you're right. She says she's coming tomorrow. I knew you were going to say that.
note: que is never dropped (unlike English "I think you're right"). Unpacks c:creo-que. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-creo-que-dice-que-a1.

title: Telling a friend what to do: ven, mira, espera, dime
es: Mira esto. Ven conmigo. Sigue derecho y voltea a la izquierda.
en: Look at this. Come with me. Go straight on and turn left.
note: Regular = él form; 8 irregulars (ven, ten, pon, sal, haz, di, ve, sé). PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Telling a stranger (or a group) what to do: siga, voltee, vengan
es: Siga derecho dos cuadras. Tome la TransMilenio. Pasen, sigan.
en: Go straight two blocks. Take the TransMilenio. Come in, come in.
note: Colombia uses usted widely; ustedes is the only plural. Taught as "the opposite vowel" before the subjunctive exists. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: To whom, for whom: le, les (le pregunto, les explico)
es: Le pregunté al señor dónde estaba la estación. ¿Les explico el camino?
en: I asked the man where the station was. Shall I explain the way to you?
note: Doubling with a + name is normal (le dije a Vale). PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Adding detail with que: el señor que vende arepas
es: El señor que vende arepas es mi vecino. La receta que encontré es de 1975.
en: The man who sells arepas is my neighbour. The recipe I found is from 1975.
note: que for people and things; never dropped.

title: Why and so: porque, como, por eso, así que
es: Como llovía, no salimos. No tengo plata, por eso no voy. Estoy cansado, así que me voy.
en: As it was raining, we didn't go out. I have no money, that's why I'm not going. I'm tired, so I'm leaving.
note: como (cause) goes first; porque goes second. PCIC/programmes place this at A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Where the little words go: lo voy a comprar = voy a comprarlo
es: Lo voy a pensar. = Voy a pensarlo. ¿Me estás escuchando?
en: I'm going to think about it. Are you listening to me?
note: Before the conjugated verb or glued to the infinitive/gerund; both correct. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-pronombres-posicion-a2. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): moved from session 144 (A2) to 130 (u14): voy a llamarte / te voy a llamar, quiero verte.

title: "Is" for what it's like vs "is" for how it is right now: es aburrido / está aburrido
es: Don Hernando es muy tranquilo, pero hoy está nervioso.
en: Don Hernando is very calm, but today he's nervous.

forms.es: Don Hernando es muy tranquilo, pero hoy está nervioso.
forms.en: Don Hernando is very calm, but today he's nervous.
The soup is delicious.
The class is boring.
I'm bored.

note: Big five. Weight reading toward estar. Meaning-changers: aburrido, listo, rico, malo, vivo. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-ser-estar-adjetivos-a2.

title: The state something is in: está cerrado, está roto, estoy preocupado
es: La máquina está dañada. La puerta estaba abierta. Estamos muy preocupados.
en: The machine is broken. The door was open. We're very worried.
note: Participle agrees like an adjective.

title: More "backwards" verbs: me parece, me queda, me cae bien, me hace falta
es: Me parece una buena idea. Esa chaqueta te queda grande. Tu amigo me cae muy bien.
en: It seems like a good idea to me. That jacket is too big for you. I really like your friend.

title: The best, the cheapest, super-cheap: el más barato, carísimo
es: Es el café más viejo del barrio. Esos zapatos están carísimos.
en: It's the oldest café in the neighbourhood. Those shoes are really expensive.
note: de, not "in", after a superlative. -ísimo spelling (riquísimo, larguísimo).

title: Two little words together: me lo, te la, se lo
es:
¿Me empaca la camisa?
Claro, ya se la empaco.
en:
Could you wrap the shirt for me? (formal)
Of course, I'll wrap it for you right away.

forms.es:
¿Me empaca la camisa?
Claro, ya se la empaco.
forms.en:
Could you wrap the shirt for me? (formal)
Of course, I'll wrap it for you right away.
Will you lend it to me?
I'll send it to you tomorrow.

note: le/les → se before lo/la. Comprehension first; production lags. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: If… then: si quieres, vamos; si llueve, me quedo
es: Si quieres, vamos al cine.
en: If you want, we'll go to the cinema.

forms.en: If you want, we'll go to the cinema.

forms.es: Si llueve, nos quedamos en casa.
forms.en: If it rains, we'll stay at home.

forms.es: Si ves a Vale, dile que la llamo.
forms.en: If you see Vale, tell her I'll call her.

title: When, while, every time: cuando, mientras, siempre que + present or past
es: Cuando llego, Vale ya está aquí. Mientras yo cocinaba, él lavaba. Cuando era niño, vivía en Toronto.
en: When I arrive, Vale is already here. While I was cooking, he was washing up. When I was a kid I lived in Toronto.
note: Only habitual/past cuando here; cuando + future meaning waits for the subjunctive (g:subj-cuando-future). Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): cuando + present for habits is licensed from session 80 by p:cuando-basic; this lesson is cuando / mientras / siempre que across the pasts.

title: For and by, part 1: para (destination, purpose, deadline) vs por (through, because of, per)
es: Salimos para Medellín por la mañana. Gracias por todo. Es para el viernes.
en: We leave for Medellín in the morning. Thanks for everything. It's for Friday.
note: Rules of thumb only; second pass at B1, third at B2. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): para (purpose, recipient) is licensed from session 25 by p:para-inf; por stays here.

title: Commands with the little words: dímelo, siéntese, tráiganmelo
es: Siéntese, por favor. Dímelo. Bájese en la próxima. Tráiganmelo mañana.
en: Sit down, please. Tell me. Get off at the next one. Bring it to me tomorrow.
note: Glued on in positive commands, with an accent to keep the stress. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-pronombres-posicion-a2.

title: Mine, yours, his: mío, tuyo, suyo (un amigo mío)
es:
¿Esta maleta es suya?
No, la mía es la roja.
en:
Is this suitcase yours? (formal)
No, mine is the red one.

forms.es:
¿Esta maleta es suya?
No, la mía es la roja.
forms.en:
Is this suitcase yours? (formal)
No, mine is the red one.

forms.es: Un amigo mío vive en Santa Marta.
forms.en: A friend of mine lives in Santa Marta.
That mobile is yours, isn't it?

title: People in general: se habla, se vende, se necesita, se puede
es: Se necesita mesero. Aquí se habla inglés. ¿Se puede pagar con tarjeta?
en: Waiter needed. English spoken here. Can you pay by card?
note: Plural agreement with plural things (se venden arepas). PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Where, who and the thing that: donde, quien, lo que
es: Es el lugar donde trabajé. Lo que necesito es tiempo. Es la persona con quien hablé.
en: It's the place where I worked. What I need is time. She's the person I spoke with.
note: lo que = "what" in statements (not qué).

title: When Spanish says "the" and English doesn't (and the reverse)
es: Me gusta el café. Soy ingeniero. Los lunes trabajo. Juego al fútbol. Es la una.
en: I like coffee. I'm an engineer. On Mondays I work. I play football. It's one o'clock.
note: General statements take the article; no article with professions after ser; el agua.

title: Guessing out loud: ¿Dónde estará? Serán las tres. Tendrá unos sesenta años.
es: ¿Dónde estará Simón? Estará con Don Hernando. Serán las once.
en: Where can Simón be? He's probably with Don Hernando. It must be about eleven.
note: In LatAm speech the -ré future is mostly for guesses. Forms are taught here through the guess use: one set of endings on the whole infinitive, twelve short stems (tendr-, pondr-, sabr-, habr-…). PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Promises, predictions and formal plans: te llamaré, lloverá, será difícil
es: Te prometo que volveré. Mañana lloverá en Bogotá. No será fácil.
en: I promise I'll come back. Tomorrow it will rain in Bogotá. It won't be easy.
note: ir a stays the default for plans; -ré for promises, forecasts, written plans and the news. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Would: me encantaría, podrías, deberías, and yo que tú
es: Me encantaría ir.
en: I'd love to go.

forms.en: I'd love to go.
Could you help me?
You should rest.
If I were you, I wouldn't sign.

note: Same stems as the future. Unpacks c:me-gustaria and c:podria. SEQ new lesson(s): fn-cortesia-condicional-a1. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Wanting someone else to do something: quiero que vengas
es: Quiero que trabajes conmigo. Necesito que me ayudes. Prefiero que lo hablemos.
en: I want you to work with me. I need you to help me. I'd rather we talk about it.
note: The subjunctive enters with ONE trigger (wanting) and the "opposite vowel" forms they already know from usted commands. Different subject → que + subjunctive; same subject → infinitive. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: The irregular "wish" forms: sea, vaya, tenga, haga, sepa, esté, haya
es: Quiero que seas sincero. Necesito que vayas al banco. Espero que haya tiempo.
en: I want you to be honest. I need you to go to the bank. I hope there's time.
note: Built on the yo form (tengo → tenga) plus six true irregulars. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-formulas-subjuntivo-a2. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Telling someone not to: no toques, no se preocupe, no lo hagan
es: No toques eso. No se preocupe. No me digas. No lo firmen todavía.
en: Don't touch that. Don't worry. You don't say. Don't sign it yet.
note: Pronouns go BEFORE the verb in negative commands. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Wishing: ojalá, espero que, que te vaya bien
es: Ojalá no llueva. Espero que te guste. ¡Que te mejores! ¡Que les vaya bien!
en: I hope it doesn't rain. I hope you like it. Get well soon! Good luck, all of you!
note: Unpacks c:ojala and c:que-te-mejores. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-formulas-subjuntivo-a2. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Reacting: ¡Qué bueno!, ¡Qué pena!, ¡Qué tan lindo!, ¡Cuánta gente!
es: ¡Qué bueno verte! ¡Qué casa tan bonita! ¡Cuánto tiempo!
en: How good to see you! What a lovely house! Long time no see!
note: ¡Qué + noun + tan/más + adj! Accent marks on exclamative qué/cuánto. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): ¡Qué + adjective! is licensed from session 23 by p:exclamations-basic; this lesson is ¡Qué tan…!, ¡Cuánto…!, ¡Qué … tan …!

title: Making it small and friendly: un tintico, ahorita, un momentico
es: ¿Me regala un tintico? Espérame un momentico. Ahorita voy.
en: Could I have a little coffee? Wait a moment. I'm coming (in a bit).
note: Colombia: -ico after t (momentico, ratico, gatico); -ito elsewhere. Warmth and politeness, not only size. ahorita = soon/now depending on region.

title: What or which: ¿qué? vs ¿cuál?
es: ¿Cuál es tu número de celular? ¿Qué quieres tomar? ¿Cuál prefieres?
en: What's your phone number? What would you like to drink? Which one do you prefer?

title: Some, any, none: algún, alguien, algo, ningún, nadie, nada
es: ¿Hay algún problema?
en: Is there a problem?

forms.en: Is there a problem?
I don't have any complaints.
Does anyone know anything?

note: alguno/ninguno shorten before a masculine noun. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): algo / alguien are licensed from session 23 by p:indefinites-basic; this lesson is algún / ningún / alguno and agreement.

title: How long it's been going on: hace un año que…, desde hace…, llevo…
es: Hace tres meses que vivo aquí.
en: I've lived here for three months.

forms.es: Hace tres meses que vivo aquí.
forms.en: I've lived here for three months.

forms.es: Trabajo aquí desde hace un año.
forms.en: I've worked here for a year.
I've been waiting for an hour.

note: English present perfect → Spanish PRESENT here.

title: But and but rather: pero vs sino (no es caro, sino barato)
es: No es colombiano, sino canadiense. No quiero té sino café. Es caro, pero vale la pena.
en: He isn't Colombian but Canadian. I don't want tea, I want coffee. It's expensive, but it's worth it.
note: sino que before a verb.

title: Even though: aunque + a fact
es: Aunque es tarde, el café está lleno. Aunque no me gusta, lo hago.
en: Even though it's late, the café is full. Even though I don't like it, I do it.
note: aunque + subjunctive (hypothetical) waits until B2 (g:subj-concessive). PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: As much as, as many as: tanto como, tanta gente, igual de
es: Trabajo tanto como tú. No hay tantos clientes como antes. Es igual de caro.
en: I work as much as you. There aren't as many customers as before. It's just as expensive.

title: Saying who twice: le di el libro a Vale
es: Le di la llave a Vale. ¿Le dijiste a tu mamá? A mí me parece bien.
en: I gave the key to Vale. Did you tell your mom? I think it's fine.

title: How you do it: -mente (rápidamente, realmente) and other ways to say how
es: Habla lentamente. Realmente no sé. Lo hizo rápido y bien.
en: She speaks slowly. I really don't know. He did it quickly and well.
note: Feminine form + -mente; keeps the accent. In speech LatAm often uses the adjective (habla rápido).

title: Telling what someone said: me dijo que estaba cansado, me preguntó si…
es: Me dijo que estaba cansado.
en: He told me he was tired.

forms.en: He told me he was tired.
I asked her if she wanted to come.

forms.es: Me contó que se iba a Cali.
forms.en: She told me she was going to Cali.

note: Only the easy shifts: present → imperfect, ir a → iba a. Backshift with había/vendría at B1. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: By doing, while doing: aprendí leyendo, sigue lloviendo, va mejorando
es: Aprendí español viendo novelas. Sigue lloviendo. El café va mejorando.
en: I learned Spanish by watching soaps. It's still raining. The café is getting better.
note: Gerund = by/while -ing; never as a noun (Nadar es bueno, not *Nadando es bueno).

title: Keeping a story in order: primero, luego, al final, ese día, al día siguiente
es: Ese día llegué tarde.
en: That day I arrived late.

forms.en: That day I arrived late.
The next day, everything changed.

forms.es: Dos semanas después, volví a Bogotá.
forms.en: Two weeks later, I went back to Bogotá.
First I had breakfast and then I went out.

note: Shifts deixis (hoy → ese día, mañana → al día siguiente); needed for reported speech. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): primero / luego / después / al final are licensed from session 32 by p:time-sequence-basic; this lesson is the longer story frame.

title: Just, already, still, not yet: acabo de, ya, todavía, ya no
es: Acabo de llegar. ¿Ya comiste? Todavía no. Ya no trabajo allá.
en: I've just arrived. Have you eaten yet? Not yet. I don't work there any more.
note: LatAm: ¿Ya comiste? (preterite) is the everyday form; unpacks c:ya-comiste. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): ya / todavía / ya no / todavía no are licensed from session 52 by p:ya-todavia-basic; this lesson is acabar de and the fine points.

title: Messages, emails and reviews: openings, closings and usted in writing
es: Estimada señora Ruiz:
en: Dear Mrs Ruiz,

forms.en: Dear Mrs Ruiz,
I am writing to ask you for some information.
I look forward to your reply. (written by a woman)
Hugs,

note: Punctuation of letters (colon after the greeting), usted forms in formal mail.

title: So that: para + verb vs para que + someone else
es: Te escribo para pedirte un favor. Te escribo para que me ayudes.
en: I'm writing to ask you a favour. I'm writing so that you'll help me.
note: Same rule as quiero / quiero que. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Reacting to what others do: me alegra que, me molesta que, qué bueno que
es: Me alegra que estés aquí.
en: I'm glad you're here.

forms.en: I'm glad you're here.
It's great that you came!
It's great that you came!
It bothers me that he arrives late.

note: Same "backwards" verbs as gustar, now with que + subjunctive. Present-reference only. PCIC/programmes place this at B1; taught at A2 here.

title: I think so / I don't think so: creo que es… vs no creo que sea…
es: Creo que tienes razón.
en: I think you're right.

forms.en: I think you're right.
I don't think you're right.
I think so.

forms.es: No me parece que sea justo.
forms.en: I don't think it's fair.

note: Big five. Statement = indicative; denial = subjunctive.

title: Judging: es importante que, es mejor que, es normal que, es una pena que
es: Es importante que lo leas. Es mejor que esperemos. Es una pena que cierren.
en: It's important that you read it. It's better for us to wait. It's a shame they're closing.
note: Es verdad/cierto/obvio que + indicative (a fact) vs value + subjunctive.

title: The good thing, the worst part: lo bueno, lo malo, lo mejor es que
es: Lo bueno es que tenemos clientes. Lo peor fue la espera. Lo importante es seguir.
en: The good thing is we have customers. The worst part was the wait. What matters is to keep going.

title: Doubt and possibility: dudo que, es posible que, puede que
es: Dudo que Altamira cambie de idea. Es posible que llueva. Puede que tengas razón.
en: I doubt Altamira will change his mind. It might rain. You may be right.
note: subjunctive refers to present or future here.

title: Maybe: quizás, tal vez + either mood; a lo mejor + fact form
es: Quizás venga mañana.
en: Maybe he'll come tomorrow.

forms.en: Maybe he'll come tomorrow.
Maybe he's ill.
Maybe you're right.

note: a lo mejor always indicative; quizás/tal vez: subjunctive = less sure.

title: Guessing about the past: serían las diez, tendría veinte años
es: Serían las diez cuando llegó. Tendría unos veinte años. ¿Por qué lo haría?
en: It must have been about ten when he arrived. She'd have been about twenty. Why would he have done it?

title: Feelings about what others do, fully: me da miedo que, me sorprende que, siento que
es: Me da miedo que vendan el edificio. Me sorprende que no lo sepas. Siento que te sientas así.
en: I'm scared they'll sell the building. I'm surprised you don't know. I'm sorry you feel that way.
note: Same subject → infinitive (me alegra verte).

title: Becoming: ponerse nervioso, quedarse callado, volverse famoso, hacerse rico
es: Me puse rojo. Se quedó callado. Se volvió muy serio. Quiere hacerse médico.
en: I went red. He went quiet. He became very serious. She wants to become a doctor.
note: ponerse = sudden mood/colour; quedarse = result; volverse = character; hacerse = effort/career. PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: When "se" changes the meaning: ir and irse, dormir and dormirse, quedar and quedarse
es: Me voy.
en: I'm off.

forms.en: I'm off.
I fell asleep in the meeting.
We stayed at home.

forms.es: Quedamos en vernos a las seis.
forms.en: We agreed to meet at six.

note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): quedarse, acordarse, dormirse… are licensed from g:reflexive-routine (76) as vocabulary; this lesson teaches the meaning contrasts (dormir / dormirse, ir / irse).

title: Had already happened: había llegado, ya se habían ido
es: Cuando llegué, Vale ya se había ido. Nunca había visto tanta gente.
en: When I arrived, Vale had already left. I had never seen so many people.

title: Telling a story with all your pasts: what happened, what it was like, what had happened before
es: Era domingo. Tomás abrió la caja que había encontrado y vio una carta.
en: It was Sunday. Tomás opened the box he had found and saw a letter.
note: Foreground/background; the LatAm perfecto only for open-ended experience. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-pasados-repaso-b1.

title: Reporting further back: dijo que había llamado, que vendría
es: Dijo que había llamado tres veces. Prometió que vendría. Me explicó que no lo sabía.
en: She said she had called three times. He promised he would come. He explained that he didn't know.

title: Advising and asking: te recomiendo que, te pido que, le aconsejo que
es: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado. Le pido que me escuche. No dejes que te asuste.
en: I recommend you talk to a lawyer. I'm asking you to listen to me. Don't let him scare you.
note: Indirect object + que + subjunctive.

title: When it happens (it hasn't yet): cuando llegues, en cuanto sepa, hasta que vuelva
es: Cuando llegues, llámame. En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso. No me voy hasta que vuelva.
en: When you arrive, call me. As soon as I know anything, I'll let you know. I'm not leaving until he comes back.
note: antes de que always subjunctive.

title: Purpose and plans for others: para que, sin que, antes de que
es: Lo dejo aquí para que lo veas.
en: I'll leave it here so you can see it.

forms.es: Lo dejo aquí para que lo veas.
forms.en: I'll leave it here so you can see it.

forms.es: Salió sin que nadie lo viera.
forms.en: He left without anyone seeing him.

forms.es: Sale sin que nadie lo note.
forms.en: He leaves without anyone noticing.
Call me before you leave.

note: Present-tense frames only at this point.

title: Looking for one that…: busco un local que tenga ventanas
es: Buscamos un local que tenga cocina.
en: We're looking for premises that have a kitchen.

forms.es: Buscamos un local que tenga cocina.
forms.en: We're looking for premises that have a kitchen.

forms.es: ¿Conoces a alguien que sepa de leyes?
forms.en: Do you know anyone who knows about law?

forms.es: No hay nada que podamos hacer.
forms.en: There's nothing we can do.

note: Known thing = indicative; unknown/non-existent = subjunctive.

title: Relatives after a preposition: el local en el que, la gente con la que, a quien
es: Es el edificio en el que nació mi abuela. La persona a quien le escribí no contestó.
en: It's the building my grandmother was born in. The person I wrote to didn't answer.
note: Spanish never strands the preposition. PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Each, any at all: cada, cualquier, cualquiera, todo, toda
es: Cada mesa tiene su historia.
en: Each table has its story.

forms.en: Each table has its story.
Anyone can come.
Any of them will do.

title: It just happened to me: se me olvidó, se me cayó, se nos dañó
es: Se me olvidaron las llaves. Se le cayó el celular. Se nos dañó la nevera.
en: I forgot my keys. She dropped her phone. Our fridge broke down.
note: The thing is the subject; the person is the indirect object. Very common in Colombia. PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Body parts and belongings without "my": me duele la espalda, le robaron el celular
es: Me corté el dedo. Le robaron la billetera. Me lavo el pelo.
en: I cut my finger. They stole his wallet. I wash my hair.

title: Hoping or doubting it has happened: espero que hayas llegado bien
es: Espero que no se haya perdido. No creo que lo hayan leído. Me alegra que hayas venido.
en: I hope he hasn't got lost. I don't think they've read it. I'm glad you came.
note: In LatAm this also covers the recent finished past under a trigger (Me alegra que hayas venido). PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: For and by, part 2: por for time, means and exchange; para for opinion and comparison
es: Lo tomas tres veces por día.
en: You take it three times a day.

forms.es: Lo tomas tres veces por día.
forms.en: You take it three times a day.
For me, it's serious.

forms.es: Para ser lunes, hay mucha gente.
forms.en: For a Monday, there are a lot of people.
I exchanged it for another one.

note: SEQ new lesson(s): gr-por-para-b1.

title: General advice and rules: hay que, se debe, uno tiene que, conviene
es: Hay que tomar mucha agua. No se debe fumar aquí. Uno nunca sabe.
en: You need to drink lots of water. Smoking isn't allowed here. You never know.

title: Should, must, must be: debes, deberías, debe de ser
es: Debes descansar. Deberías ir al médico. Debe de estar cansada.
en: You must rest. You should see a doctor. She must be tired.
note: deber de = conjecture (formal); everyday speech often uses deber for both — accept both, teach the distinction. Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): deber + infinitive in the present is now taught (and tagged) with g:tener-que-hay-que at 82; this lesson is deberías and debe de (probability).

title: Things done (who did it doesn't matter): se vendieron, se construyó, se firmarán
es: Se vendieron todos los almuerzos. El edificio se construyó en 1920. Se firmará el lunes.
en: All the lunches were sold. The building was built in 1920. It will be signed on Monday.

title: Comparing in numbers and degrees: el doble, más de la mitad, cada vez más, cuanto más…
es: Ganamos el doble que el año pasado.
en: We earn twice as much as last year.

forms.es: Ganamos el doble que el año pasado.
forms.en: We earn twice as much as last year.
There are more and more tourists.
The more I work, the less I sleep.

title: So, therefore, so much that: por lo tanto, de modo que, tan… que
es: Las ventas bajaron; por lo tanto, cerramos los lunes.
en: Sales fell; therefore, we close on Mondays.

forms.es: Las ventas bajaron; por lo tanto, cerramos los lunes.
forms.en: Sales fell; therefore, we close on Mondays.

forms.es: Estaba tan cansado que se durmió.
forms.en: He was so tired that he fell asleep.

forms.es: Llovió mucho, de modo que nos quedamos en casa.
forms.en: It rained a lot, so we stayed at home.

title: Questions with a preposition first: ¿con quién?, ¿de qué?, ¿para qué?, ¿a qué hora?
es: ¿Con quién hablaste? ¿De qué se trata? ¿Para qué sirve esto?
en: Who did you talk to? What's it about? What's this for?
note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): ¿de dónde?, ¿con quién?, ¿a qué hora?, ¿por qué?, ¿para qué? are licensed from session 18 by p:prep-questions-basic; this lesson is the verb-governed ones (¿De qué se trata? ¿En qué piensas? ¿Con qué sueñas?).

title: Passing on requests: dice que vengas, me pide que lo llame
es: Vale dice que la llames. Mi mamá me pide que vaya el domingo. Dile que espere.
en: Vale says to call her. My mom is asking me to go on Sunday. Tell him to wait.
note: decir que + indicative = report; + subjunctive = request.

title: Asking politely and reporting questions: ¿sabe si…?, no sé dónde…, quería saber cuándo…
es: ¿Sabe si está abierto?
en: Do you know if it's open? (formal)

forms.en: Do you know if it's open? (formal)
I don't know where I left it.
I wanted to know how much it costs.

note: Accent stays on the question word.

title: The news voice: fue construido, serán juzgados, está prohibido
es: El edificio fue declarado patrimonio. Los responsables serán investigados.
en: The building was declared heritage. Those responsible will be investigated.
note: Mostly written/news; speech prefers se or ellos. PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Giving causes in writing: ya que, puesto que, debido a, a causa de, por + verb
es: Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame. Cerraron debido a la lluvia. La multaron por no tener permiso.
en: Since you're here, help me. They closed because of the rain. They fined her for not having a permit.

title: Despite: a pesar de, a pesar de que, sin embargo, aun así
es: A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.
en: Despite the rain, they came.

forms.es: A pesar de la lluvia, vinieron.
forms.en: Despite the rain, they came.

forms.es: Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.
forms.en: It's expensive; however, it's worth it.
Even so, I'm not signing.

title: Doing things as subjects: fumar es malo, me encanta cocinar, el no saber
es: Cocinar para tanta gente no es fácil. Me molesta tener que esperar.
en: Cooking for so many people isn't easy. Having to wait bothers me.
note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): a plain infinitive as subject (Bailar es divertido) is licensed by g:verb-infinitive (24); this lesson is el + infinitive and infinitives inside emotion frames.

title: Organising a text: en primer lugar, además, por un lado… por otro, en resumen
es: En primer lugar, el local es nuestro.
en: Firstly, the premises are ours.

forms.es: En primer lugar, el local es nuestro.
forms.en: Firstly, the premises are ours.
What's more, the neighbourhood supports us.

forms.es: Por un lado, es caro; por otro, es muy bonito.
forms.en: On the one hand, it's expensive; on the other, it's very nice.
In short, we're not selling.

title: Not repeating yourself in a text: este, ese, aquel, dicho, el mismo, lo anterior
es: El alcalde y el concejal hablaron; este dijo que no había presupuesto.
en: The mayor and the councillor spoke; the latter said there was no budget.

forms.es: El alcalde y el concejal hablaron; este dijo que no había presupuesto.
forms.en: The mayor and the councillor spoke; the latter said there was no budget.
The project in question was approved.

forms.es: Lo anterior no significa que vayamos a cerrar.
forms.en: The above does not mean that we are going to close.

title: The "if only" forms: fuera, tuviera, pudiera (from the past form)
es: Si tuviera plata, compraría el edificio. Ojalá pudiera ayudarte.
en: If I had money, I'd buy the building. I wish I could help you.
note: Built from ellos preterite (tuvieron → tuviera). -ra for production; -se recognised (g:se-form-recognition). PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: If things were different: si fuera… sería…
es: Si fuera tú, hablaría con ella.
en: If I were you, I'd talk to her.

forms.es: Si fuera tú, hablaría con ella.
forms.en: If I were you, I'd talk to her.

forms.es: Si no lloviera, abriríamos la terraza.
forms.en: If it weren't raining, we'd open the terrace.
If I had money, I'd travel more.

note: Never conditional after si (*si tendría). PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: As if: como si fuera, como si nada
es: Habla como si fuera el dueño. Siguió como si nada.
en: He talks as if he were the owner. She carried on as if nothing had happened.
note: PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Wanting, asking, feeling in the past: quería que, me pidió que, me alegró que
es: Quería que vinieras.
en: I wanted you to come.

forms.en: I wanted you to come.
She asked me to call her.
I was glad they won.

note: Sequence of tenses: past trigger → -ra form. PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Wishing things were different: ojalá + fuera / tuviera
es: Ojalá estuvieras aquí.
en: I wish you were here.

forms.en: I wish you were here.
If only it were that easy.
I wish I had more time.

note: ojalá + present (hope) vs + -ra (wish). PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Reporting orders and requests: me dijo que fuera, les pidió que esperaran
es: Me dijo que fuera a la reunión. Les pidió que esperaran afuera.
en: He told me to go to the meeting. She asked them to wait outside.
note: PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Saying the same thing five ways: from "pásame eso" to "le agradecería que…"
es: Pásame la sal.
en: Pass me the salt.

forms.en: Pass me the salt.
Will you pass me the salt?
Could you pass me the salt? (formal)

forms.es: ¿Será que me puede pasar la sal?
forms.en: Could you possibly pass me the salt? (formal)

forms.es: Le agradecería que me enviara el documento.
forms.en: I would be grateful if you could send me the document.

note: Includes usted-to-tú negotiation and Colombian over-politeness (¿será que me puede…?).

title: Softening: quería pedirle, ¿será que…?, un poquito, me imagino que
es: Quería preguntarle algo.
en: I wanted to ask you something. (formal)

forms.en: I wanted to ask you something. (formal)
Could you possibly help me? (formal)
I imagine you're busy. (formal)

note: Imperfect of politeness, future of softening (¿será que…?, very Colombian).

title: Had it happened: hubiera llegado, hubiéramos sabido
es: Ojalá lo hubiera sabido. No creí que hubieran vendido.
en: I wish I had known. I didn't believe they had sold.

title: Would have: habría ido, lo habría hecho
es: Yo habría dicho que no. ¿Qué habrías hecho tú?
en: I would have said no. What would you have done?

title: If it had happened: si hubiera sabido, habría venido (and mixed: hoy estaría…)
es: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
en: If I had known, I would have come sooner.

forms.es: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
forms.en: If I had known, I would have come sooner.

forms.es: Si no hubiéramos firmado, hoy estaríamos tranquilos.
forms.en: If we hadn't signed, we'd be fine today.

forms.es: Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido antes.
forms.en: If I had known, I would have come sooner.

note: Colloquial LatAm also uses hubiera… hubiera (si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido): accept it.

title: Even if: aunque llueva, por más que insista
es: Aunque me ofrezcan un millón, no vendo. Por más que insista, no voy a firmar.
en: Even if they offer me a million, I'm not selling. However much he insists, I'm not going to sign.

title: Only if, unless, in case: a menos que, con tal de que, siempre que, en caso de que
es: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos. No cerramos a menos que llueva. En caso de que llamen, avísame.
en: I'll sign as long as they let us stay. We don't close unless it rains. In case they call, let me know.

title: Building an argument: es cierto que…, pero; no solo… sino también; en cambio; de hecho
es: Es cierto que necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.
en: It's true that we need money, but not at any price.

forms.es: Es cierto que necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.
forms.en: It's true that we need money, but not at any price.
In fact, sales are going up.

forms.es: No solo es barato, sino también práctico.
forms.en: It's not only cheap but also practical.

forms.es: Ellos quieren vender; nosotros, en cambio, queremos quedarnos.
forms.en: They want to sell; we, on the other hand, want to stay.

title: Guessing about what has happened: habrá salido, se habrán equivocado
es: No contesta; se habrá dormido.
en: He's not answering; he must have fallen asleep.

forms.en: He's not answering; he must have fallen asleep.
They'll have arrived by now.
Where can I have left my keys?

title: Reporting without vouching: según fuentes, el alcalde habría firmado
es: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos. El acusado estaría fuera del país.
en: According to the paper, the company allegedly paid bribes. The accused is reportedly abroad.
note: Journalistic; recognise and use in reporting. PCIC/programmes place this at C1; taught at B2 here.

title: Who did it? Hiding the doer: dicen que, se cree que, uno, la gente
es: Dicen que el alcalde renunció. Se cree que fue un error. Uno no puede saberlo todo.
en: They say the mayor resigned. It's believed it was a mistake. One can't know everything.

title: Reporting a whole conversation: tenses, times and places shift
es: "Mañana vengo" → Dijo que al día siguiente vendría. "¿Dónde está?" → Preguntó dónde estaba.
en: "I'll come tomorrow" → He said he would come the next day. "Where is it?" → She asked where it was.

title: Verbs that report and verbs that request: advertir que, recordar que, insistir en que
es: Me advirtió que era peligroso.
en: He warned me it was dangerous.

forms.en: He warned me it was dangerous.
He warned me not to go.
She insisted that we pay.

forms.es: Me recordó que la reunión era a las tres.
forms.en: He reminded me that the meeting was at three.

title: Not seeing, not noticing, not saying: no vi que…, no dijo que…, no es que…
es: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
en: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I can't.

forms.es: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
forms.en: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I can't.
I didn't notice she was angry.
He didn't say it was urgent.

title: Putting the spotlight on one part: fue Vale quien…, lo que necesito es…, aquí es donde…
es: Fue Vale quien encontró la carta.
en: It was Vale who found the letter.

forms.es: Fue Vale quien encontró la carta.
forms.en: It was Vale who found the letter.

forms.es: Lo que no entiendo es por qué.
forms.en: What I don't understand is why.
This is where it all began.

title: Starting with the topic: el contrato lo firmé yo; a Vale no le dije nada
es: El contrato lo firmé yo.
en: I'm the one who signed the contract.

forms.en: I'm the one who signed the contract.

forms.es: A Vale no le dije nada.
forms.en: I didn't tell Vale anything.
That, I didn't know.

note: A fronted object needs its pronoun.

title: How very…!: lo difícil que es, lo bien que cocina, con lo cansado que estoy
es: No sabes lo difícil que es.
en: You don't know how hard it is.

forms.es: No sabes lo difícil que es.
forms.en: You don't know how hard it is.
Your mum cooks so well!

forms.es: Con lo cansado que estoy, no voy a salir.
forms.en: Tired as I am, I'm not going out.

title: Formal relatives: el cual, la cual, lo cual, quien(es)
es: Firmaron un acuerdo, lo cual nos sorprendió. Su abuela, quien fundó el café, murió en 2019.
en: They signed an agreement, which surprised us. His grandmother, who founded the café, died in 2019.
note: Commas change meaning (explicativas). PCIC/programmes place this at C1; taught at B2 here.

title: Compact descriptions: una vez terminado, siendo tan tarde, construido en 1920
es: Construido en 1920, el edificio es patrimonio. Siendo tan tarde, preferimos esperar.
en: Built in 1920, the building is heritage. It being so late, we'd rather wait.
note: Avoid the "gerund of afterwards" (*Llegó, sentándose después).

title: Having done: después de haber firmado, por no haber llamado
es: Después de haber firmado, se arrepintió. Me multaron por no haber pagado.
en: After having signed, he regretted it. They fined me for not having paid.

title: Formal letters: le agradecería que, me dirijo a usted, adjunto le envío
es: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja. Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del viernes.
en: I am writing to you to make a complaint. I would be grateful if you replied before Friday.

title: Verbs that bring their own preposition: contar con, depender de, tratarse de, consistir en
es: Contamos con su apoyo. Depende de ti. Se trata de un error. Consiste en tres partes.
en: We count on your support. It depends on you. It's a mistake. It consists of three parts.
note: Grammar node for the principle; each verb is a pattern node.

title: Whoever, wherever, whatever: el que quiera, donde quieras, lo que sea
es: El que quiera venir, que venga. Siéntate donde quieras. Haré lo que sea necesario.
en: Whoever wants to come can come. Sit wherever you like. I'll do whatever is necessary.

title: When it would happen: dijo que me llamaría cuando llegara
es: Me dijo que me llamaría cuando llegara. Íbamos a esperar hasta que bajaran los precios.
en: He said he would call me when he arrived. We were going to wait until prices fell.

title: Que + wish or order: que entre, que lo haga él, que no se repita
es:
Está aquí el abogado.
Que entre.
en:
The lawyer is here.
Show him in.

forms.es:
Está aquí el abogado.
Que entre.
forms.en:
The lawyer is here.
Show him in.
Let him do it.
Make sure it doesn't happen again.

title: Reading Spain's Spanish: vosotros, habéis, id, os
es: ¿Vosotros qué queréis? Os lo dije. Venid mañana.
en: What do you (all) want? I told you. Come tomorrow.
note: Recognition only. Learners keep producing ustedes; Peninsular answers are accepted everywhere. PCIC/programmes place this at A1; taught at B2 here.

title: Spain's "today" past: hoy he ido = hoy fui
es: (España) Esta mañana he ido al médico. = (Colombia) Esta mañana fui al médico.
en: This morning I went to the doctor.
note: Recognition + accepted as answers; the Peninsular perfecto/indefinido split is explained, not produced. SEQ new lesson(s): gr-perfecto-vs-indefinido-a2. PCIC/programmes place this at C1; taught at B2 here.

title: The other "if only" form: hubiese, fuese, tuviese
es: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

forms.es: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
forms.en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

forms.es: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
forms.en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.
She asked me to be punctual.

note: Recognition; -se is mostly written in LatAm. Frame: Si lo hubiese sabido… = Si lo hubiera sabido…

title: Tenses that don't mean their time: quería pedirte, será caro pero…, mañana viajo
es: Quería pedirte un favor.
en: I wanted to ask you a favour.

forms.en: I wanted to ask you a favour.

forms.es: Será muy rico, pero no tiene modales.
forms.en: He may be very rich, but he has no manners.
In 1810 the act is signed.
I'm travelling to Cali tomorrow.

note: Historic present, imperfect of politeness and of plans (iba a…), future of concession.

title: Choosing the mood on purpose: el hecho de que, lo que digas, como no vengas
es: El hecho de que no llamara me preocupa. Haz lo que te digan. Como no vengas, me enojo.
en: The fact that he didn't call worries me. Do what they tell you. If you don't come, I'll get angry.

title: Distancing yourself from a claim: al parecer, supuestamente, por lo visto, no es que…
es: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
en: Apparently, the permit was fake.

forms.es: Al parecer, el permiso era falso.
forms.en: Apparently, the permit was fake.

forms.es: Supuestamente iban a demoler el edificio.
forms.en: They were supposedly going to demolish the building.

forms.es: No es que dude de ti.
forms.en: It's not that I doubt you.

title: Saying it again, better: o sea, es decir, mejor dicho, en otras palabras
es: Es caro; o sea, no lo podemos pagar.
en: It's expensive; I mean, we can't afford it.

forms.es: Es caro; o sea, no lo podemos pagar.
forms.en: It's expensive; I mean, we can't afford it.
Or rather, we don't want to pay for it.

forms.es: Es decir, el proyecto se cancela.
forms.en: That is, the project is cancelled.

title: Saying it with force: ¡si ya te lo dije!, ¡qué va!, ¡pues claro que sí!
es: ¡Si ya te lo dije! ¿Que si me gusta? ¡Me encanta! ¡Pues claro que voy!
en: But I already told you! Do I like it? I love it! Of course I'm going!

title: Wishes and regrets as exclamations: ¡quién lo hubiera dicho!, ¡si lo hubiera sabido!
es: ¡Quién lo hubiera dicho! ¡Si al menos llamara! ¡Ojalá nunca lo hubiera firmado!
en: Who would have thought it! If only he'd call! I wish I'd never signed it!

title: Whose: cuyo, cuya (and how people avoid it)
es: El edificio, cuyos dueños viven en Miami, será vendido.
en: The building, whose owners live in Miami, will be sold.

title: Turning actions into nouns: la firma del contrato, el cierre, la toma de decisiones
es: Tras la firma del contrato, se anunció el cierre del local.
en: After the contract was signed, the closure of the premises was announced.

title: Once done: una vez firmado el contrato, terminada la reunión, dicho esto
es: Una vez aprobado el plan, comenzarán las obras. Dicho esto, pasemos al siguiente punto.
en: Once the plan is approved, work will begin. Having said that, let's move on.

title: Conceding like a writer: si bien, aun cuando, por mucho que, por muy… que
es: Si bien el plan es ambicioso, es viable.
en: Although the plan is ambitious, it is feasible.

forms.es: Si bien el plan es ambicioso, es viable.
forms.en: Although the plan is ambitious, it is feasible.

forms.es: Por muy rico que sea, no puede comprarlo todo.
forms.en: However rich he may be, he can't buy everything.

forms.es: Por mucho que insistas, no voy a ir.
forms.en: However much you insist, I'm not going.
Even if it rains, we'll go out.

title: Results in writing: de ahí que, de manera que, así pues, por consiguiente
es: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazara.
en: There was no agreement; hence the meeting was postponed.

forms.es: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazara.
forms.en: There was no agreement; hence the meeting was postponed.

forms.es: Así pues, la decisión es nuestra.
forms.en: Thus, the decision is ours.

forms.es: Llegó tarde, de manera que perdió el vuelo.
forms.en: He arrived late, so he missed the flight.

forms.es: Por consiguiente, se suspende la obra.
forms.en: Consequently, the works are suspended.

note: de ahí que + subjunctive.

title: Conditions with style: de haberlo sabido, como no llegues, a no ser que, siempre y cuando
es: De haberlo sabido, no habría venido. Como no llegues a tiempo, nos vamos sin ti.
en: Had I known, I wouldn't have come. If you're not on time, we're leaving without you.

title: Fine comparisons: cuanto más… menos, ni que fuera, más vale que
es: Cuanto más lo pienso, menos lo entiendo.
en: The more I think about it, the less I understand it.

forms.es: Cuanto más lo pienso, menos lo entiendo.
forms.en: The more I think about it, the less I understand it.
As if he were the president!
You'd better get here early.

title: Exact timing: nada más llegar, apenas, en cuanto, una vez que, a medida que
es: Nada más llegar, se fue la luz. A medida que avanzaba la noche, llegaba más gente.
en: As soon as we arrived, the power went out. As the night went on, more people arrived.

title: Agreement when sense beats grammar: la mayoría piensa(n), el resto, la gente
es: La mayoría de los vecinos votó (votaron) en contra. Un grupo de turistas llegó.
en: Most of the neighbours voted against. A group of tourists arrived.

title: Ser and estar at the edges: está de mesero, es de madera, estar para, estar por
es: Ahora está de mesero en Cartagena.
en: He's working as a waiter in Cartagena now.

forms.es: Ahora está de mesero en Cartagena.
forms.en: He's working as a waiter in Cartagena now.
The table is made of wood.
It's about to rain.
That remains to be seen.

note: SEQ new lesson(s): gr-ser-estar-adjetivos-a2.

title: Hearing paisas (and Argentines): vos tenés, vos sabés, vení
es: ¿Vos qué querés? Vení, sentate. ¿Sabés qué?
en: What do you want? Come, sit down. You know what?
note: Recognition only (Medellín story dialogue); never required in production. Also usted among family in Bogotá/Boyacá.

title: Old and legal Spanish: quien hiciere, si así fuere
es: El que no cumpliere será sancionado. Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres.
en: Whoever fails to comply will be penalised. When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
note: Recognition only (legal texts, proverbs).

title: Word order for effect: Mucho ha cambiado el barrio; poco importa ya
es: Mucho ha cambiado el barrio desde entonces.
en: The neighbourhood has changed a lot since then.

forms.es: Mucho ha cambiado el barrio desde entonces.
forms.en: The neighbourhood has changed a lot since then.
It's hard to say.
It hardly matters now.

title: Commenting on your own sentence: lamentablemente, francamente, por suerte, sinceramente
es: Lamentablemente, el café cerró. Francamente, no me sorprende. Por suerte, nadie salió herido.
en: Sadly, the café closed. Frankly, I'm not surprised. Luckily, nobody was hurt.
note: Placed with the critical-review unit where it does most work. PCIC/programmes place this at B2; taught at C1 here.
